channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Orders Review of All Railway and Domestic Flight Schedules
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has instructed officials to review and revise all railway and domestic flight schedules within one month. The directive also emphasizes activating negotiations with foreign airlines to utilize the "fifth freedom of the air" regime.

item.title: Nearly 16,000 Personal Assistants in Kyrgyzstan Receive Food Aid
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, 15,846 personal assistants caring for disabled children and adults have received food aid totaling 1,949 tons. Each family received a package including 100 kg of wheat flour, 10 liters of vegetable oil, and 12.5 kg of peas. This aid is part of the UN World Food Programme's strategic plan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Proposes Extending Mortgage Relief for Borrowers
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank suggests extending a special mortgage rule until 2029. This rule allows individuals to obtain mortgages even if their loan payments exceed half of their income. The bank will still assess repayment ability, but the strict debt-to-income ratio may be relaxed for some.

item.title: Russians Challenge Multi-Million Ruble Recycling Fees on Cars from Kazakhstan
item.description: Russian citizens are contesting substantial recycling fee charges on vehicles manufactured in Kazakhstan. The Supreme Court of Russia has requested case materials related to these disputes, which involve not only the fee amounts but also the application of a compensation formula for cars assembled in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Exempt Individuals from Income Tax on Written-Off Problem Debts
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to exempt individuals from personal income tax (PIT) on written-off problem debts from loans and microloans. The Tax Code implementation project office approved the amendment. This aims to alleviate the burden on borrowers by treating forgiven debt amounts as non-taxable income within certain limits.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Beef Exports Projected to Increase by One-Third by 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan's beef exports are anticipated to see a significant rise, with projections indicating a one-third increase by the year 2026. This growth is expected to bolster the country's agricultural trade sector.

item.title: Mortar Shell Explosion at Religious School in Farah Kills Four Students
item.description: An explosion of a mortar shell at a religious school in the Bakwa district of Farah province, Afghanistan, has resulted in the deaths of four students and injuries to two others. The incident occurred when students found the shell and brought it into the school, where it detonated.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Rules for Calculating Interest on Loans and Deposits
item.description: Kazakhstan will implement new regulations from November 30th for calculating the annual effective interest rate on loans and deposits. Financial institutions must display the actual rate prominently, not in small print. They will also be obligated to recalculate the effective rate upon a client's request. Islamic banks and interbank transactions are exempt.

item.title: Astana Car Reseller Sentenced to Nearly Seven Years for $103 Million Fraud
item.description: A car reseller in Astana has been sentenced to nearly seven years in prison for defrauding car owners of over 103 million tenge. The reseller convinced victims to remotely transfer vehicle ownership under the guise of selling them for car loans, then kept the proceeds. The court found him guilty of six counts of large-scale fraud.

item.title: Central Asian Banks Seek Measurable AI Business Results Beyond Experiments
item.description: The FINNEXT Asia forum in Tashkent focused on how Central Asian banks can achieve tangible business results from AI, moving beyond pilot projects. Discussions included data security, accountability, and making Islamic finance more competitive through digital technology. One bank presented its new AI platform aimed at improving overall business performance.

item.title: Two Kazakhstan Airports Seek Manager to Handle Billion-Tenge Debts
item.description: Airports in Taldykorgan and Usharal, managed by Zhetysu airline, are seeking a new manager to address significant debts totaling 4.3 billion tenge accumulated over previous years, plus a 770 million tenge loss in 2025. The new manager will be responsible for repaying aircraft debts, investing in airport development, and expanding flight routes.

item.title: High-Voltage Power Line Failure Causes Electricity Outages in Bishkek
item.description: A 110-kilovolt high-voltage power line, 'CHP-Parkovaya-2', experienced a break in Bishkek at 17:31, leading to widespread electricity disruptions. Specialists are working on-site to restore power, with the cause of the failure still under investigation. Residents in several districts reported power outages.

item.title: Almaty Intensifies Efforts to Prevent Juvenile Delinquency
item.description: Almaty is strengthening measures to prevent juvenile delinquency, aligning with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's emphasis on law and order and legal culture among youth. Educational institutions are implementing the 'Adal Azamat' program to foster values like honesty and responsibility. Joint preventive work with law enforcement is underway.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Congratulates Oman's Sultan on National Day, Recalls Visit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent a congratulatory telegram to Sultan Haitham bin Tarik of Oman on the Sultanate's National Day. Tokayev recalled the Sultan's recent historic visit to Kazakhstan, noting it was the first by an Omani head of state and strengthened bilateral strategic partnership. The visit in October marked 35 years of diplomatic relations.

item.title: Uzbekistan and USA Advance Tourism with New Visa-Free Agreement and Investment Deals
item.description: Uzbekistan and the United States are enhancing tourism exchanges, with a visa-free regime for US citizens set to begin January 1, 2026. Direct flights between Tashkent and New York and increased American tourist numbers highlight growing bilateral ties. This follows meetings and agreements, including significant Uzbek purchases of Boeing aircraft and planned investments.

item.title: Beeline Uzbekistan Owner Aims for Banking License in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan
item.description: VEON, the parent company of Beeline Uzbekistan, plans to obtain banking licenses in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. The company already offers financial services and sees banking as a strategic growth area, aiming to integrate telecom and financial products.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Tashkent Region Enters New Development Phase with Focus on Economy and Tourism
item.description: The Tashkent region is undergoing significant socio-economic development, with projects in industry, investment, agriculture, and tourism. Following President Mirziyoyev's visit on June 18, 2025, priorities include leveraging natural resources, boosting tourism infrastructure, and creating jobs. Industrial output is projected to increase by the end of 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ranks 32nd in UN E-Government Development Index, Entering 'Very High EGDI' Category
item.description: Uzbekistan has achieved 32nd place in the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI), entering the 'Very High EGDI' group for the first time. The country has climbed 55 positions since 2020 and 31 since 2024. Its EGDI score is 0.8930, with strong performance in online services, telecom infrastructure, and human capital.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes New Regulations for Import, Testing, and Sale of GMOs
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering new regulations for the import, testing, use, and sale of genetically modified organisms (GMOs). The Ministry of Environment has drafted a bill introducing three risk levels, mandatory safety assessments, and a permit system for specific activities. The proposal categorizes products into low, medium, and high-risk levels.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Mandatory Housing Insurance for Natural Disasters
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to implement mandatory insurance for apartments and private homes against natural disasters. Residents may pay annual premiums ranging from 2,000 to 22,000 tenge. Compensation will be provided from an insurance fund for properties damaged by earthquakes, floods, or forest fires.

item.title: Head of Transport and Logistics Department of Presidential Administration Dismissed
item.description: Azamat Keskinbayev has been dismissed from his position as head of the Transport and Logistics Development Department of the Presidential Administration of Kazakhstan. The dismissal was announced by the press service of Akorda. This follows recent changes in the National Security Committee leadership.

item.title: Afghan and Indian Traders Sign $250 Million in Trade Agreements
item.description: Afghan and Indian traders have signed trade cooperation agreements totaling $250 million in New Delhi. The agreements aim to expand trade relations, increase Afghanistan's exports, and create new business opportunities, focusing on dried fruits and agricultural products. Banking cooperation was also strengthened.

item.title: Electricity from Uzbekistan Becomes Significantly Cheaper for Kazakhstan
item.description: In January-September 2026, Kazakhstan imported 476.2 million kWh of electricity from Uzbekistan for $20.99 million, with an average cost of 4.41 US cents per kWh. This is cheaper than the 4.6 cents per kWh recorded in the same period of 2025. Kazakhstan continues to be a major importer of electricity from Russia.

item.title: Tokayev Dismisses Head of Transport and Logistics Department in Presidential Administration
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed Azamat Keskinbayev from his position as Head of the Department for the Development of the Transport and Logistics Industry within the Presidential Administration. Keskinbayev had held the role for less than a year. The reasons for his dismissal and his new role are currently unknown.

item.title: Atyrau Entrepreneurs Scale Up: From Small Business to New Opportunities
item.description: Three Atyrau companies, China Talk, VOLTIX, and ACCEL ERLANOVNA, are undergoing transformation with support from the Shell LiveWIRE program, a joint initiative by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and Shell Kazakhstan. The program provides training and expert support to help entrepreneurs improve management, implement digital solutions, and foster further growth, contributing to regional economic diversification.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Proposes Expanding Migros Supermarkets in Regions
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has invited Turkey's Anadolu Group to develop Migros supermarket chains in the Samarkand and Khorezm regions. He noted the high demand for modern supermarkets and urged the Turkish side to expedite concrete proposals with regional authorities. This initiative aims to introduce modern, digitized retail networks, starting with these two regions before expanding elsewhere.

item.title: Azamat Keskinbayev Dismissed from Presidential Administration Post
item.description: By decree of the President of Kazakhstan, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Azamat Keskinbayev has been relieved of his position as Head of the Transport and Logistics Development Department of the Presidential Administration. Keskinbayev had held the post since December 23, 2025.

item.title: Prince Charles' 1996 Central Asia Tour: A Kazakh Chapan and Diplomatic Outreach
item.description: In November 1996, Prince Charles visited Ukraine, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan shortly after their independence. In Kazakhstan, then-President Nursultan Nazarbayev presented him with a traditional chapan robe. The tour aimed to expand UK diplomatic presence and affirm the sovereignty of the newly independent nations.

item.title: Almaty Hospitals See Surge in Children with Viral Infections and High Fevers
item.description: Parents in Almaty are reporting an increase in viral infections among children, with fevers reaching up to 40°C. Many children have been hospitalized with symptoms including vomiting, diarrhea, and weakness. The city's infectious disease hospital has seen a significant rise in young patients.

item.title: New Tashkent-Parkent Electric Railway Line Enhances Regional Transport Capabilities
item.description: A new electrified railway line connecting Tashkent and Parkent district has opened, improving regional transport. The 24-kilometer line, built at a cost of 535.4 billion UZS, includes a new station and bridges. Modern electric trains now operate on the route.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan Border Guards Meet in Osh to Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Border guards from Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan held their eighth joint Military Council meeting in Osh, reporting no incidents on their shared border since early 2026. Discussions focused on managing increased passenger and cargo flows, combating cross-border crime, and addressing threats from drones and AI.

item.title: Uzbekistan: AI-92 Gasoline Price Hits Record on Exchange
item.description: The price of AI-92 gasoline on the Uzbek Republican Commodity and Raw Material Exchange has reached a new record, exceeding 15 million soms per ton. The AI-92 K2-L grade saw a daily increase of 2.3%, trading at 15.25 million soms per ton. This specific grade was offered in the largest volume, with most of it being purchased by buyers.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Dollar Trades at 455.3 Tenge on Exchange
item.description: The average weighted exchange rate of the US dollar on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange rose by 6.19 tenge to 455.32 tenge by the end of trading on Friday. The national currency weakened by 6.2 tenge during the trading session.

item.title: Tajikistan's Trade Deficit Widens 53% as Imports Surge
item.description: Tajikistan's trade deficit grew by 53% to $7.06 billion in the first ten months of 2026, driven by a 41.2% surge in imports to $9.42 billion. Exports rose 15.2% to $2.36 billion. Vehicle imports nearly doubled, accounting for over a quarter of the increase. Remittances likely kept the current account in surplus.

item.title: Tajik President Rahmon Briefs Putin on Afghan Border Security Situation
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon discussed the security situation along the Afghan border with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The Kremlin reported that the leaders addressed smuggling and drug trafficking, emphasizing the need for continued cooperation between border services and intelligence agencies to manage cross-border challenges.

item.title: Construction Sites in Bishkek Inspected, Warnings Issued by Ministry
item.description: The Department of State Architecture-Construction Control in Kyrgyzstan has conducted inspections of construction sites across the country. The ministry reported that checks focused on compliance with approved project documents, urban planning requirements, and construction norms. Several warnings were issued regarding adherence to regulations and site beautification.

item.title: Four Sentenced in Alatau City for Embezzling Funds Without Working
item.description: Four individuals have been sentenced in Alatau city for embezzling budget funds. Prosecutors discovered that two employees of the Career Center illegally calculated salaries from the budget for individuals who did not actually work. The state incurred a loss of 6 million tenge. The embezzled funds have been fully reimbursed.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts International Congress 'Man and Medicine' for First Time
item.description: Dushanbe, Tajikistan, hosted the International Congress 'Man and Medicine – Tajikistan' on November 19, 2026, marking the 35th anniversary of the CIS. The event, held within the CIS Year of Health, was organized by Russian and Tajik health ministries. This marked the first time the congress, a leading medical platform for over 30 years, was held internationally outside Russia.

item.title: KazMunayGas Plans to Spend 4.2 Billion Tenge on Five-Year Vehicle Lease
item.description: KazMunayGas is seeking to lease 34 vehicles, including four-wheel-drive pickups, for five years at a cost of approximately 4.2 billion tenge (excluding VAT). The tender, divided into three lots for different fields, aims to secure vehicles manufactured no earlier than five years prior to the service year. The contract is set to run from January 2027 to December 2031.

item.title: Uzbek Journalist Saidabdulaziz Yusupov Sentenced to 10 Years for Inciting Constitutional Overthrow
item.description: Saidabdulaziz Yusupov, former acting director of Uzbekistan's Public Foundation for the Support and Development of Independent Media, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison. A military court found him guilty of attempting to overthrow the constitutional order and defamation. This is not Yusupov's first conviction; he previously served time for fraud.
